issues.title: Perfect HT: replicate group states (K=4) to break same-state dependency chains
issues.hypothesis: PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY is 1.50s CPU for 58.8M rows (~25ns/row, 8 aggregates) in profile.md. q01 has 4 groups with skew (N,O ~49%, A,F/R,F ~25% each). In RowOperations::UpdateStates -> UnaryScatter, every row of a group does a read-modify-write on the same state address, so all rows of one group form a serial chain through store-to-load forwarding (~4-6 cycles per link, longer for avg's hugeint add with carry). Out-of-order execution only overlaps the different groups, so throughput is limited by the largest group: about 0.49 x 5 cycles per row per aggregate. E0001 changed the loop structure, partitioning rows by group, and that overhead made it slower. This change keeps the existing vectorised scatter unchanged and only changes the addresses: row i goes to replica (i & 3) of its group. That splits each chain into 4 independent chains. Measured with dbe-tool sql (single runs): group by the 2 keys with count(*) alone spends 0.45s CPU in the perfect HT, so the per-row state update cost is high even for a single aggregate.
issues.plan:
In src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp and the header src/include/duckdb/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.hpp:
(1) Add a member `idx_t replica_count`, set in the constructor. It is 4 when ALL aggregates have function.order_dependent == AggregateOrderDependent::NOT_ORDER_DEPENDENT, none is DISTINCT, and total_groups * tuple_size * 4 <= ~1MB (use a constant). Otherwise it is 1. Also mark avg as NOT_ORDER_DEPENDENT in extension/core_functions/aggregate/algebraic/avg.cpp (GetAverageAggregate / the decimal binder BindDecimalAvg must keep it, so set it on the returned function after the bind replaces it). avg is order-independent in the same sense sum already is.
(2) Allocate and InitializeStates for total_groups * replica_count tuples. Replica r occupies the tuple indexes [r*total_groups, (r+1)*total_groups). group_is_set keeps only total_groups entries.
(3) AddChunk: keep the group computation and the bounds check. Then set address_data[i] = data + (group + (i & (replica_count-1)) * total_groups) * tuple_size. Leave the rest unchanged (UpdateStates, AddInPlace, filtered path).
(4) Combine(other): for each set group i, and for each replica r of `other`, combine the source tuple (r*total_groups+i) into the target tuple i (the target's replica 0). Batch these into the existing source/target address vectors. Before the global table is used (Combine and Scan run on gstate.ht in physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp:170/196), the target's own replicas >0 must either be empty or be folded in. Simplest: the global table also receives AddChunk? Check: it does not, so it only gets Combine into replica 0. Still, add a private FoldReplicas() that combines replicas 1..K-1 into 0 for set groups. Call it at the start of Scan (once, guarded by a flag) and on `other` at the start of Combine, to be robust.
(5) Destroy(): call destructors on all total_groups*replica_count tuples whose group is set (index i % total_groups), or simply on all replicas of set groups.
issues.expected_gain: q01: PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY 1.5s -> ~0.9-1.1s CPU, roughly 8-15% wall. If the chain theory is wrong, the change is neutral (extra init of 4x states, negligible).
issues.generality: Any low-cardinality GROUP BY on small-range integer or compressed-string keys with sum/count/avg/min/max-style aggregates (the perfect HT path). The more skewed and the fewer the groups, the bigger the gain. Order-dependent aggregates (list, string_agg, first/arg_min ties) are excluded by the gate, so their results are unchanged. Possible slowdown: perfect HTs with many groups (more init and combine work); the size cap limits this.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Correctness depends on combine being correct for all gated aggregates, which parallel execution already relies on. Floating-point sums may differ in the last bits, as they already can across threads. Make sure group_is_set and Destroy cover all replicas so there are no leaks with arena-allocated states.

dispatch: Perfect HT: replicate group states (K=4) to break same-state dependency chains
output.memory:
# Memory

## Workload
- Single visible template q01 = TPC-H Q1 shape: scan lineitem with one range filter on a date (selects ~98%),
  4 groups (2 string keys -> compressed to utinyint), 4 sum_no_overflow + 3 avg + count_star on DECIMAL(int64).
- Bench ~332-342ms. Operator CPU (profile, summed over threads): TABLE_SCAN 2.0-2.5s, PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY 1.45-1.72s,
  projections ~0.2 + 0.04 + 0.17s.
- Storage (pragma_storage_info): l_quantity/extendedprice/discount/tax/shipdate = BitPacking; returnflag/linestatus = Dictionary
  (old dictionary compression, 978 segments, ~61K rows each).
- Types: l_* decimals DECIMAL(15,2) int64; products still int64; sums run as sum_no_overflow (int64 state).
  avg on decimal int64 uses AvgState<hugeint_t> AddToHugeint (sum_helpers.hpp:109). avg is NOT marked NOT_ORDER_DEPENDENT; sum/count are.
- Group distribution: N,O 49%, A,F 25%, R,F 25%, N,F <1% -> skewed, randomly interleaved.

## Key measurements (dbe-tool sql, single runs, noisy; the machine is slow, ~6-8ns/value/column CPU everywhere)
- Q1 with filter ~680ms; no filter ~480ms; no filter + max(l_shipdate) ~555ms -> filter path costs >=18%.
- count(*) with only the date filter: 71ms; adding 4 more trivial filters on the decimal cols: 265ms.
- sum of 4 decimal cols, no filter 225ms, with date filter 350ms.
- group by returnflag,linestatus count(*): ~180-207ms; EXPLAIN ANALYZE: scan 0.86s CPU, perfect HT 0.45s CPU (count only!),
  compress_string projection 0.02s (it runs on the dictionary only). group by 1 key: 134ms.
- No single anomalous operator in the scan; string dict scan costs about the same as bitpacked int scan per value.

## Codebase facts
- Scan with filters: RowGroup::Scan (src/storage/table/row_group.cpp ~694-829). Filter cols -> StandardColumnData::Filter
  (standard_column_data.cpp:76): uses compression->filter if present, else ColumnData::Filter = Scan + ToUnifiedFormat +
  ColumnSegment::FilterSelection. Other cols -> StandardColumnData::Select -> compression->select if present, else
  ColumnData::Select = full Scan + result.Slice(sel) => DICTIONARY vectors downstream.
- Compression funcs with select: constant, RLE, dict_fsst, validity. NOT bitpacking, not old Dictionary. No bitpacking filter.
- Old dictionary scan: src/storage/compression/dictionary_compression.cpp:144 emits DictionaryVector when scan_count==2048,
  decompression in src/storage/compression/dictionary/decompression.cpp.
- fixed_size_uncompressed scan is zero-copy -> never compact scan results in place generically.
- Perfect hash agg: src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp. The constructor initializes all total_groups states. AddChunk:
  ComputeGroupLocation per key, a bounds check plus group_is_set, then UpdateStates per aggregate + AddInPlace. Combine (l.163)
  combines the local into the global via group_is_set. Scan/Destroy iterate group_is_set. Global ht only receives Combine
  (physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp:170), Scan at :196.
- AggregateFunction::order_dependent defaults to ORDER_DEPENDENT (aggregate_function.hpp:129).
- Scatter loops: src/include/duckdb/common/vector_operations/aggregate_executor.hpp.
- avg / sum impls in extension/core_functions/aggregate/{algebraic/avg.cpp,distributive/sum.cpp}.
- dbe-tool sql: selecting typeof(col) without an aggregate errors; wrap it in any_value(). EXPLAIN ANALYZE works via dbe-tool sql.
  Bash: only plain dbe-tool calls; no cd, shell variables, pipes, or chained commands.

## Round log
- G1R1: E0001 per-group simple_update in perfect HT -> RETIRED (bad idea: groups interleaved, partitioning costs more).
- G1R2: E0002 bitpacking select (flat compacted payload) -> RETIRED: neutral. Slicing is not the cost.
- G1R3: dispatched "Perfect HT: replicate group states (K=4) to break same-state dependency chains".
  Theory: all rows of one group form a serial RMW chain through memory (store-forward latency); row i -> replica i&3.
  If neutral -> the HT cost is not chain latency but instruction count / dictionary-sel indirection; then consider fused
  multi-aggregate scatter or avg int64 state.

## Ideas not yet explored / backlog
- Perfect HT: drop the 8 AddInPlace passes (per-aggregate offset), or fuse sum/avg loops (follow-up from E0001).
- avg(decimal int64) with int64 sum state when stats bound it (like sum_no_overflow), avoiding the hugeint carry chain.
- Fuse stacked projections (in backlog; needs investigation of compressed_materialization).
- Bitpacking `filter` callback (filter while decompressing). Note the date filter's count(*) costs only 71ms total, so the gain is limited.
- Decimal multiply overflow checks in projections (could skip using stats).
